subject: general
question: The length of the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle is 13 cm and the length of one of the other two sides is 5 cm. What is the area (in cm²) of the triangle?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Recognize the **Pythagorean triplet**: **5, 12, 13**.

Given **hypotenuse = 13 cm** and **one side = 5 cm**, the **other side (height) must be 12 cm**.

Area = (1 ÷ 2) × base × height = (1 ÷ 2) × 5 × 12 = 30 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 30 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Hypotenuse (h) = 13 cm, Base (b) = 5 cm.

**Formula Used:** Pythagoras Theorem: h² = b² + p² | Area = (1 ÷ 2) × b × p

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/07955eb8b318f590d7ab978632da164608ddb7da1c27f372e6c29a05c8a814ee.png] 

⇒ p² = 13² − 5²

⇒ p² = 169 − 25 = 144

⇒ p = √144 = 12 cm

⇒ Area = (1 ÷ 2) × 5 × 12

⇒ Area = 5 × 6 = 30 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 30 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Triplets

Common sets of integers that satisfy a² + b² = c² include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), and (7, 24, 25).

Area of Triangle (Heron's Formula)

For any triangle with sides a, b, and c, Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)], where s = (a+b+c) ÷ 2.

Circumradius of Right Triangle

The radius of the circumcircle of a right-angled triangle is always half of the **hypotenuse** (R = h ÷ 2).</p
